tools.pricing_summary: Free: $0 and 500 AI credits per editor each month. Team: $20/seat/month billed annually or $24 billed monthly, with 15,000 AI credits per billable collaborator each month. tools.verification_notes: Airtable's August 10, 2026 billing documentation says AI credits are pooled at workspace or organization level. Credits fund features such as Field Agents, AI automations, deep-research questions, feedback categorization, document analysis, and image generation; consumption varies by input, selected model, and output. The Airtable AI Terms, last updated July 23, 2026, classify Input and Output as Customer Data and state that customers retain all ownership rights in both. Airtable states that neither it nor its third-party AI providers will use Input, Output, or other Customer Data to train generative-AI models. For Business and Enterprise Scale, providers do not log Input or Output for human review or retain it, subject to stated exceptions. For Free, Team, Pro, and Plus workspaces, providers may retain Input and Output for up to 30 days for safety and compliance moderation.
unresolved_claims: The ownership clause does not guarantee that generated output is unique, copyrightable, or free of third-party rights.
Third-party providers may retain metadata for billing, safety, and compliance even where Input and Output retention is prohibited.
The current AI Terms still mention legacy Pro and Plus workspaces in the retention section even though the current public pricing lineup is Free, Team, Business, and Enterprise Scale.

The Privacy Policy says Bolt may use AI Inputs and Outputs to operate, maintain, and improve the service, including AI performance, reliability, and safety, using aggregated, anonymized, or de-identified data. The Privacy Policy says training/improvement opt-out controls may depend on account type or plan, while third-party AI providers process Inputs to provide services to Bolt under contractual confidentiality and data-protection obligations.
unresolved_claims: Bolt's security page says code and prompts are never used to train foundation models, while the Privacy Policy permits aggregated, anonymized, or de-identified AI content to improve AI performance and describes plan-dependent training controls. tools.verification_notes: Terms last updated February 25, 2025 say Descript claims no ownership of User Content. Inputs and AI-generated Outputs are User Content, and as between the user and Descript, the user owns them to the extent protectable under applicable law. Descript warns that outputs may not be unique or copyrightable and makes the user responsible for third-party rights and legal suitability. Descript may use Inputs and Outputs for model and service development unless the user opts out; its agreements prohibit third-party AI providers from using those Inputs and Outputs to train their own models. Current Help Center guidance is more specific: production models use no Descript user data, internal R&D uses only data from users who opted into sharing, and Enterprise sharing is disabled by default. Descript requires explicit recorded authorization from the depicted speaker before creating a custom voice clone; it refuses deceased, non-consenting, non-authorizing, or artificial-source voices. Consent source: https://help.descript.com/ai-speech/custom-speaker. Data-controls source: https://help.descript.com/account-and-app-settings/data-privacy. Premium Storyblocks media has a commercial-use license under its EULA, but other libraries may require separate clearance; GIPHY assets cannot be used commercially. The page now states the annual saving as up to 35% and names the team sizes each plan scales to.
unresolved_claims: The terms establish user ownership of protectable Output but do not provide a single universal commercial-license clause covering every generated feature and bundled asset. Commercial use therefore remains subject to third-party media licenses and applicable rights.

The privacy policy's general language allows AI training and service improvement, while newer Help Center guidance says in-house training is opt-in and production models use no user data. The exact default for a particular non-Enterprise account should be confirmed in its current Share Data setting.
AI-generated output may not qualify for copyright protection and may resemble output generated for other users.

The Free plan has no commercial license; shared Free output requires ElevenLabs attribution. All paid plans include commercial rights provided the output was generated during the paid subscription, the user holds the necessary underlying rights, and the use complies with applicable law, the Terms, Prohibited Use Policy, and Service-Specific Terms. ElevenLabs says it uses certain submitted data to improve its models, but any user can disable 'Improve the models for everyone'; the opt-out applies to newly submitted data. Enterprise data is not used for training by default except as necessary to provide the contracted service. The Prohibited Use Policy bans replicating another person's identifiable voice without consent or legal right, harmful impersonation, and deceptive failure to disclose AI generation. Policy source: https://elevenlabs.io/use-policy RE-VERIFIED 2026-11-14 at elevenlabs.io/pricing: every plan price and credit allowance matches the 2026-09-18 record, as does the two-month rollover cap. Commercial rights can vary for individual products under Service-Specific Terms, and Beta Services have no commercial rights.

tools.pricing_summary: Copilot Free is free and limited to 2,000 completions per month, auto model selection, and an unspecified allowance of GitHub AI Credits. Copilot Student is free for verified students. Paid individual plans: Pro $10/month with 1,500 total monthly AI credits; Pro+ $39/month with 7,000; Max $100/month with 20,000. Organization plans: Business $19/user/month with 1,900 AI credits per user; Enterprise $39/user/month with 3,900. Additional usage is $0.01 per AI credit; code completions and next-edit suggestions remain unlimited on paid plans.
tools.verification_notes: GitHub's Terms effective April 27, 2026 state that GitHub does not claim ownership of Copilot Input or Output. For individual licenses, GitHub and its affiliates may use Inputs and Outputs to develop, train, and improve AI/ML models unless the user opts out in account settings. The individual-license training provision does not apply when use is governed by a GitHub Customer Agreement or volume licensing agreement; those agreements control data use. GitHub says Inputs and Outputs are not shared with third-party AI model providers for those providers' independent model training. GitHub warns that Output can resemble training data or third-party/open-source code. Users must determine whether a license is required and review, test, and validate Output. GitHub's broader Terms grant GitHub and its affiliates rights to use hosted user content to develop and train AI technologies; the Copilot opt-out does not apply to public-repository content or the broader repository-content license. Re-verified 2026-10-01: The official Copilot plans documentation still matches the recorded Free/Pro/Pro+/Max and Business/Enterprise prices and AI-credit allocations; no drift detected. RE-VERIFIED 2026-11-14 at docs.github.com/copilot plans: Pro $10/month, Pro+ $39/month, Max $100/month, Business $19/seat/month, Enterprise $39/seat/month; Pro includes 1,500 AI credits (1,000 base + 500 flex), Pro+ 7,000 (3,900 + 3,100), Max a 10,000 base plus 20,000 flex, and overage is $0.01 per credit. Copilot Standalone for GitHub Enterprise Cloud users without a GHEC licence is $10/user/month. No recorded fact changed.
unresolved_claims: GitHub does not publish a numeric AI-credit allowance for Copilot Free or Student on the plans page.
The public Terms do not give a blanket commercial-use warranty, non-infringement guarantee, or ownership assignment for generated Output; they only state that GitHub does not claim ownership.
Starting April 22, 2026, new self-serve Copilot Business sign-ups for organizations on GitHub Free and GitHub Team were temporarily paused; the official page did not publish an end date.

unresolved_claims: No current official Make AI-specific provision assigning ownership of generated output to the customer was verified; the general Master Services Agreement is therefore not presented as an output-rights guarantee.

The no-training statements were verified for Make AI Toolkit and Maia, but a single universal statement covering every Make AI feature, every connected third-party provider, and every customer configuration was not found.
The AI Toolkit statement that Make does not store data must be read alongside its explicit statement that interaction logs are retained in scenario logs for 30 days.

AI Agent functionality and pricing remain subject to beta-era changes where the applicable documentation labels the feature beta.

No recorded fact changed.
unresolved_claims: The general pricing page does not expose one comprehensive price for every Microsoft Copilot product or enterprise licensing scenario.

tools.verification_notes: Official pages confirm AI features including Notion Agent, Custom Agents, Enterprise Search, AI Meeting Notes, Research Mode, AI writing, translation, file/image analysis, and database creation. By default, Notion and its AI subprocessors do not use Customer Data to train models; subprocessors are contractually prohibited from doing so. Some data-retaining LLM features may be enabled by workspace administrators. Deleted pages/workspaces can be restored for 30 days and are then deleted, including AI-generated data and embeddings. Notion states that it does not claim ownership of inputs or outputs; both are treated as Customer Data. Outputs may not be unique. Supplementary terms were last updated July 27, 2026. RE-VERIFIED 2026-11-14 at notion.com/pricing: Free $0, Plus $10/member/month, Business $20/member/month, Enterprise custom; Notion AI agents free to try then $10 per 1,000 monthly credits. No recorded fact changed.
unresolved_claims: Notion does not publicly disclose the exact numerical limits for its rolling six-hour or monthly AI usage allowances.
The exact credit consumption rate for each Custom Agent action varies by operation and is not fully specified on the general pricing page.

tools.pricing_summary: basic: Free; 300 monthly transcription minutes, 30 minutes per conversation, and three lifetime audio/video file imports. pro: $16.99/user/month monthly or $8.33/user/month billed annually; 1,200 in-app recording minutes, up to 90 minutes per meeting, 10 monthly file imports, and unlimited storage. business: $30/user/month monthly or $19.99/user/month billed annually; unlimited meetings and in-app recordings, up to four hours per meeting, unlimited file imports subject to the shared-pool note, three concurrent meetings, and enhanced administration. enterprise: Custom quote; includes SSO, SCIM, domain capture, Otter API/webhooks, enterprise controls, custom integrations, and optional HIPAA compliance.
tools.verification_notes: The repository's Basic allowance of 300 minutes per month and Pro limit of 1,200 minutes are still supported. The repository's Business price of $30/user/month is the monthly rate, but the official annual rate is currently $19.99/user/month. Otter's official Privacy & Security page says it automatically trains proprietary models on de-identified recordings and transcripts; the data is encrypted and not manually reviewed as part of that automatic method. A separate Feedback and Training setting allows users to permit or revoke Otter and third-party-provider access to conversations for training and product improvement, including human review. Selecting 'Don't allow sharing' removes access to past conversations and excludes future conversations under that setting. Otter states that its external AI service providers do not train on or retain customer data sent through their APIs. Customers retain ownership of User Content and grant Otter a service-operating license. Workspace or organization administrators may own and control data placed under an organizational account, including migrated pre-existing data. Users are solely responsible under the terms for legally required recording notices and consent. Otter also provides pre-meeting notices, in-meeting announcements, and an Enterprise Microsoft Teams affirmative-permission flow. RE-VERIFIED 2026-11-14 at otter.ai/pricing: Basic free with 300 monthly minutes; Pro $16.99/month or $8.33/month billed annually; Business $30/month or $19.99/month billed annually; Enterprise custom. No recorded fact changed.
unresolved_claims: Otter's official materials describe both automatic de-identified model training and settings-based training permissions. Do not reduce this to a blanket 'no training' or blanket 'opt-out' claim without clarifying which processing path and account tier is meant.
The pricing page displayed temporary Business promotional pricing alongside standard monthly and annual rates; promotional figures should not be presented as durable list pricing.

tools.pricing_summary: Official support lists Standard/Free, individual Pro, individual Max, Enterprise Pro, and Enterprise Max. Max includes everything in Pro plus the highest access to advanced models, Comet Max Assistant, Create files and apps, and Brain. The reviewed public consumer-plan pages did not expose current Pro or Max dollar prices. An official organization-onboarding article lists Enterprise Pro at $40/seat monthly or $400/seat annually.
tools.verification_notes: Perplexity is documented as an AI-powered answer/search product with citations, premium models, file uploads, Research, Create files and apps, Comet, and Computer features depending on plan. AI Data Retention is enabled by default for Free, Pro, and Max users and can be turned off for future collection; previously collected training data is not removed by a later opt-out. Enterprise data is not used for AI training, and Perplexity says its third-party model-provider agreements prohibit provider training on Perplexity data. Consumer terms warn that output may be subject to third-party model licenses and use restrictions. 2026-09-02 official blog “Optimizing On-Device Inference for Apple Silicon” (https://www.perplexity.ai/hub/blog/optimizing-on-device-inference-for-apple-silicon): Lily is a lightweight local inference engine built specifically for Apple silicon and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B so on-device compute does not bottleneck Hybrid Compute / Perplexity Computer tasks. Official facts from that post: Rust runtime; OpenAI-compatible chat-completions API; custom Metal kernels; neither PyTorch nor MLX in the execution path; standalone demo on GitHub. The official pplx-garden README names the demo at https://github.com/perplexityai/pplx-garden (lily/), Apache-2.0, greedy generation for the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MLX affine 4-bit checkpoint format, Apple GPU family 10 or later (M5 and newer). Lily is not a new paid Perplexity plan SKU. Consumer Pro/Max dollar prices were not re-verified on 2026-09-02. Re-verified 2026-10-01: the official plan-comparison article still routes consumer Pro and Max to the app rather than publishing dollar amounts, and lists Education Pro at $10/mo with SheerID verification. Enterprise Pro is stated as starting at $40/month or $400/year per seat, matching the 2026-08-25 record.
unresolved_claims: Current public prices for individual Pro and Max were not verifiable from the reviewed official pages.
A blanket commercial-use or output-ownership claim was not made because consumer outputs may be governed by third-party model licenses.
Enterprise Max pricing was not publicly stated in the reviewed sources.

The official Lily blog says the chat-completions API streams tokens; the official lily README in pplx-garden as of 2026-09-02 documents stream: false and rejects streaming. Treat serving-surface details as demo-specific until re-checked.

Lily hardware support is stated as Apple GPU family 10 or later (M5 and newer) and macOS 26 or later in the official demo README; support on every later Apple chip or OS was not independently verified.

tools.pricing_summary: Poe offers free daily points and annual subscriptions of $49.99/year for 10,000 points/day, $199.99/year for 660,000 points/month, $499.99/year for 1.65 million points/month, $999.99/year for 3.3 million points/month, and $2,499.99/year for 8.25 million points/month. Poe displays annual equivalents of $4.17, $16.67, $41.67, $83.33, and $208.33 per month. Taxes, currency conversion, regional availability, and app-store pricing may vary.
tools.verification_notes: Poe provides one interface for third-party text, image, audio, and video bots, custom bots/apps, group chats, and shared subscriptions. Fully shaded privacy-shield bots share data with model providers but interactions are not used by those providers for training; half-shaded bots/apps may share data with developers or external resources and may use interactions for training. Poe's terms define prompts and bot-generated results as 'Your Content' and state that users retain ownership, while granting Poe a perpetual license for stated service purposes. Use also remains subject to policies of the underlying model providers. RE-VERIFIED 2026-11-14 at poe.com/subscription_plans: Annual plans $49.99 to $2,499.99/year across 10,000 points/day through 8.25 million points/month. No recorded fact changed.
unresolved_claims: Monthly-billing prices were not included in the extracted official pricing page, so only verified annual prices and their displayed monthly equivalents are reported.
No blanket commercial-use assurance was found because Poe grants a personal right to use the service and underlying model-provider policies may impose additional restrictions.
Privacy and training treatment varies by each bot or app's privacy-shield status.

tools.pricing_summary: Official US pricing checked 2026-10-25: Core $20/month ($18/month billed annually) with up to 30 hours of Agent chat on Free Mode, up to 60 projects and $20 towards most powerful models; Pro $100/month ($90 billed annually) with 10 parallel agents, up to 15 collaborators and 28-day database rollback; Enterprise is custom (custom seat limits, SSO/SAML, single-tenant). The public table lists only Core, Pro and Enterprise. The free Starter tier from the 2026-08-21 check is off the page. Re-verified 2026-10-25 from replit.com/pricing.
tools.verification_notes: Official documentation describes Replit Agent as turning plain-language requests into apps, designs, slides, and other artifacts. The Commercial Agreement states that commercial customers retain all rights in Input Content and own Output Content. Under the Commercial Agreement, Replit will not use Customer Content to develop or improve products, train machine-learning models, or create derivative works except as expressly permitted; customer-requested tuning may be performed solely for that customer's use during the agreement term. The consumer Terms state that users retain their rights in content they submit and grant Replit the operational rights needed to provide the service. Replit's Privacy Policy was last updated August 3, 2026 and covers collection of usage, interaction, project, command, payment, and communication data, along with applicable access, deletion, correction, appeal, and sale/sharing opt-out rights.
unresolved_claims: The explicit Output Content ownership and no-training language is in the Commercial Agreement. The general consumer Terms do not publish an equally explicit assignment of rights in AI-generated Output.
The pricing page labels free and included Agent allowances qualitatively rather than publishing exact numeric Agent-credit limits.
Third-party AI services are excluded from the Commercial Agreement's definition of Replit AI Features and can be governed by separate provider terms.

tools.pricing_summary: Creative plans: Free $0 with 125 one-time credits and 5 GB storage; Standard $15 monthly or $12/month billed annually with 625 credits/month; Pro $35 monthly or $28/month billed annually with 2,250 credits/month and 500 GB storage; Max $95 monthly or $76/month billed annually with 9,500 credits/month and up to one month of credit rollover; Enterprise has custom pricing and credits. Standard and Pro subscription credits do not roll over; purchased credits do not expire. The pricing page states Gen-4.5 costs 12 credits per generated second.
tools.verification_notes: Official pricing and Help Center pages agree on the 625/2,250/9,500 monthly credit allocations. Terms last updated May 11, 2026 state that Runway does not claim ownership of Inputs or Outputs and does not restrict commercial use of Outputs, subject to compliance with the agreement. The same terms grant Runway a perpetual license to use Inputs and Outputs for model training, labeling, classification, moderation, and related improvement. The privacy policy says submitted voice and face characteristics may be biometric data and are used only to provide the requested biometric-enabled feature. Runway's official voice-verification documentation requires explicit, in-app consent from the same speaker before custom-voice training and prohibits non-consensual replicas. Terms also prohibit impersonation and submitting another person's photograph without permission. Official voice-consent source: https://help.runwayml.com/hc/en-us/articles/29828787723411-Voice-verification RE-VERIFIED 2026-11-14 at runwayml.com/pricing: Free $0 with 125 one-time credits; Standard $15/month or $12/month annual with 625 credits; Pro $35/month or $28/month annual with 2,250 credits; Max $95/month or $76/month annual; Enterprise custom. Gen-4.5 still costs 12 credits per generated second. No recorded fact changed.
unresolved_claims: The self-serve terms authorize training on Inputs and Outputs, while Runway separately advertises no training on Enterprise customer data. The precise Enterprise exceptions depend on the separate Enterprise agreement and cannot be generalized to self-serve plans.
The pricing page does not provide a fixed Enterprise price or credit allocation.

tools.pricing_summary: Free: $0. Pro: $7.25/user/month when paid annually or $8.75 when paid monthly. Business+: $15/user/month annually or $18 monthly. Enterprise+ uses sales-based pricing. Workflow-generated summaries stored in messages or canvases follow the organization's retention settings. Admins can disable or restrict native AI features. No recorded fact changed.

Slack does not publish a single numeric usage allowance for all AI features; some capabilities state that plan limits apply.
No explicit, AI-output-specific ownership statement was located in the checked official Slack sources.

tools.pricing_summary: Checked 2026-11-03 at https://www.synthesia.io/pricing. Basic is $0 per month with 500 credits/month. Starter is $9 for the first month and $19 per month after that, with 1,250 credits/month. Pro is $49 for the first month and $89 per month after that, with 6,000 credits/month. The served page also lists higher monthly credit rungs on the Pro card and a yearly toggle that says save up to 4 months. It does not print the 2026-09-18 figures of $29 Starter, $18 yearly, 1,200 Starter credits, $64 Creator yearly, or 14,500 and 44,000 yearly credits. Enterprise pricing is custom. No rollover rule is stated.
tools.verification_notes: Customer Terms effective July 20, 2026 say the customer owns Customer Data, including Inputs and Outputs, while Synthesia owns Synthesia Content. Customers receive a limited license to Synthesia Content during the subscription and, after termination, to the extent that content was incorporated into generated videos, subject to continuing compliance. The terms license Customer Data to Synthesia only as reasonably necessary to provide, maintain, and improve the services, address security/support issues, comply with law, prevent fraud, or as expressly authorized in writing. The privacy policy generally describes Synthesia as processor of Customer Data under customer instructions. Personal-avatar documentation requires a live consent recording matching the person shown; stock avatars are based on actors who consented. The Acceptable Use Policy prohibits rights violations, deceptive impersonation, and disabling provenance mechanisms. It restricts paid social advertising with Stock Avatars unless Synthesia gives express written consent; Custom Avatar advertising requires appropriate consent from the depicted individual. Stock-avatar use in sensitive endorsement-like contexts, news, politics, or current-events content is also restricted. Acceptable-use source: https://www.synthesia.io/legal/acceptable-use-policy
unresolved_claims: The pricing page is internally inconsistent: its annual cards display Starter at $18/month and Creator at $64/month, while its FAQ states $264/year for Starter and $804/year for Creator. Those annual totals do not equal the displayed monthly equivalents, so no corrected value was inferred.

The reviewed public terms permit use of Customer Data to improve the services but do not clearly state whether that includes general model training, nor do they identify a self-serve training opt-out. A stronger no-training claim could not be verified.
Commercial use is not unrestricted: Stock Avatar advertising and sensitive-context uses can require written consent, an Enterprise plan, or both.

tools.pricing_summary: Free is $0. New accounts get a one-time $5 signup credit and a 7-message daily limit; existing Free accounts keep a recurring $5 monthly credit. Legacy Premium is $20/month and is closed to new signups. Plus is $30 per user per month with $30 monthly credits. Business is $100 per user per month with the same $30 monthly credit allowance, plus training-data opt-out and team controls. Enterprise is custom. Monthly credits expire after 65 days. Purchased credits expire after one year and lock if the paid plan lapses. Checked 2026-10-25 on v0.app/docs/pricing.
tools.verification_notes: Official documentation describes v0 as an AI agent for producing full-stack apps and agents, with Git integration, a full editor, previews, backend connections, and Vercel deployment. v0 may use user prompts or generated content with third-party models and learning systems to improve products. Enterprise content and content from customers who opt out in Vercel settings are not used for training. Vercel platform-service customer data or code is not used to train, improve, or fine-tune v0 models. The FAQ says Vercel does not own code generated from user prompts, while warning that output may resemble other output or third-party IP and must be evaluated by the user. Pricing terminology on the retrieved current documentation uses 'Plus'; some indexed official snippets still use the former name 'Team'. Business at $100 per user per month includes the same $30 monthly credit allowance as Plus.
unresolved_claims: The official page says model token rates can be viewed in the model selector or pricing page, but the extracted live documentation did not consistently expose a complete current rate table.
The FAQ does not promise copyrightability, uniqueness, non-infringement, or an IP indemnity for generated code.
The effect of deleting content already incorporated into a trained model is limited: the FAQ says existing models will not be updated after such a deletion request.

Commercial-use confirmation located in official support expressly concerns the API, not every consumer-chat use case.

In AI by Zapier, Standard model steps consume 1 task per run, Advanced 3 tasks, and Premium 5 tasks; tool calls add task usage. The pricing page separately lists Agents Free with up to 400 automated activities/month and Agents Pro with up to 1,500 activities/month, but did not expose a dependable Agents Pro price in the retrieved official page text.
tools.verification_notes: AI by Zapier supports built-in models or a connected customer AI-provider account, structured output fields, knowledge sources, and app actions as tools. Zapier's April 9, 2026 Terms define Inputs and Outputs as Customer Content and state that customers retain ownership of Customer Content. Zapier receives a limited license needed to provide, maintain, operate, improve, and support the service. Zapier may derive de-identified data sets from Customer Content and use them to improve products, including through model training. Customers may submit the linked opt-out form; Company and Enterprise accounts are automatically opted out under the current Terms. Usage Information may be used to develop and improve Zapier products, but the current clause does not explicitly say that Usage Information is used for model training. RE-VERIFIED 2026-11-14 at zapier.com/pricing: Free $0 with 100 tasks/month, Professional from $19.99/month billed annually, Team $69/month billed annually, Enterprise custom. No recorded fact changed.
unresolved_claims: The official AI by Zapier help page is internally inconsistent about Free-plan access: its availability panel marks Free unavailable, while a later section discusses the Standard tier on a Free plan.
A current official Agents Pro dollar price was not reliably exposed in the retrieved pricing-page text.
Zapier's Terms do not promise that AI output is unique, copyrightable, or non-infringing.
Third-party model handling depends on Zapier's AI Functionality Subprocessors and, for bring-your-own-model configurations, the selected provider's terms.
